claim.quote: No significant modulation signal was observed and 90% confidence level upper limits of $1.6 \times 10^{-33}$ cm$^2$ at 0.5 GeV was set for the DM-nucleon cross section. This is the first experimental result of a search for DM mediated by the bremsstrahlung effect.

key_value.note: DM-nucleon cross-section upper limit at 0.5 GeV, 90% CL.

name: Search for sub-GeV dark matter by annual modulation using XMASS-I detector

summary.plain: XMASS searched for dark matter lighter than a proton by looking for the faint extra radiation it would produce when scattering, and saw no yearly modulation.
summary.technical: 0.32-1 GeV dark matter via inelastic nuclear scattering with bremsstrahlung emission down to 1 keV electron-equivalent; 2.8 years live time (2.38 ton-years); 1.6e-33 cm^2 at 0.5 GeV; also multi-GeV (4-20 GeV) elastic search with a 2.3 keV nuclear-recoil threshold, 2.9e-42 cm^2 at 8 GeV.

title: Search for sub-GeV dark matter by annual modulation using XMASS-I detector
why_it_matters: The abstract calls it the first experimental search for dark matter mediated by the bremsstrahlung effect.
